prose.text: A time interval is a named schedule (days of the week and one time-of-day period) that a ZIA rule can reference so it applies only at certain times ([[zia.time-intervals.schema]]). "Why did this rule fire, or not fire, at that hour?" takes five questions in order.

steps.label: Does this rule type take a time at all?
steps.text: Most do; SSL Inspection is disputed: [[zia.time-intervals.rule-usage]].

steps.label: Which clock is used?
steps.text: The user's configured location, or the edge's clock for remote users and Client Connector: [[zia.time-intervals.timezone]], with the location's own time zone in [[zia.locations.model]].

steps.label: What does the interval actually contain?
steps.text: Minutes from midnight, a day list, and a single period: [[zia.time-intervals.schema]].

steps.label: What happens outside the window?
steps.text: The rule is skipped and evaluation moves on: [[zia.time-intervals.evaluation]], and the first-match rule in [[zia.url-filtering.rule-order]].

steps.label: Is it a time interval or a time window?

prose.text: Limits on counts, per-rule caps and name characters are in [[zia.time-intervals.limits]]; the API operations, update behavior and activation are in [[zia.time-intervals.api-surface]].
